title: Successful Logon
description: An account successfully logged on. The primary event for confirmation of authentication to a machine.
operator_context: Investigate unexpected logons, especially with Logon Type 10 (RDP) from non-workstation IPs, or privileged accounts at odd hours. Correlate with 4625 events before or after.

title: Failed Logon
description: An account failed to log on. The leading indicator for brute-force, credential-stuffing, and password spray attacks.
operator_context: Cluster by Source Network Address and account name. High frequency within a short window indicates brute force; act before 4740 lockouts follow. Block the source IP.

title: Logoff
description: An account logged off. Complements the 4624 logon to build a complete session record.
operator_context: Used to build session duration timelines. A logoff without a corresponding logon may indicate shared/borrowed credentials.

title: User Initiated Logoff
description: A user initiated a logoff. Indicates a clean, user-driven session termination.
operator_context: Compare with 4800 lock events. Unexpected interactive logoffs outside working hours can indicate remote administration or compromise.

title: Explicit Credential Logon
description: A logon was attempted with explicit credentials (RunAs / PSEXEC / scheduled task with stored password).
operator_context: Frequently used by attackers for lateral movement (e.g., PsExec, scheduled task dropping). Investigate the process using the secondary logon and its target host.

title: Special Privileges Assigned
description: A logon was granted special (administrator) privileges, typically SeDebugPrivilege, SeTcbPrivilege, or SeImpersonatePrivilege.
operator_context: Any privileged logon from a non-system account or unattended at odd hours is high value. Pair with 4624 Logon Type and 4688 to see what the privilege was used for.

title: Process Creation
description: A new process was created when process auditing is enabled. The foundation of endpoint behavior analysis.
operator_context: Look for parents spawning unusual children (Word -> PowerShell, w3wp -> cmd), encoded command lines, rundll32, regsvr32, or binaries in temp/user-writable paths. Enable command-line inclusion in audit policy.

title: Process Exited
description: A process was terminated. Complements 4688 to reconstruct process lifetimes.
operator_context: Crash-diagnosis companion for 4688. Rapid create/destroy cycles on the same path often indicate droppers or AV evasion.

title: Scheduled Task / Service Installation (Service Install)
description: A service was installed on the system (security audit view of service installation).
operator_context: Unexpected service installs are a classic persistence technique (e.g., svcmon, srv, name resembling system). Cross-check with 7045 and 4688.

title: User Right Assigned
description: A user right (privilege) was assigned to an account, e.g., SeDebugPrivilege or SeRemoteInteractiveLogonRight.
operator_context: Grants of SeDebug, SeLoadDriver, or SeTakeOwnership to non-privileged accounts are high priority. Verify intent against change management.

title: User Right Removed
description: A user right was removed from an account.
operator_context: Usually a legitimate hardening action. Verify the change and the identity performing it.

title: User Account Created
description: A user account was created on the system.
operator_context: New accounts outside the approved provisioning process are suspicious, particularly if the account is active immediately or added to admin groups (see 4732/4737).

title: User Account Enabled
description: A user account was enabled.
operator_context: Accounts re-enabled outside change windows, or immediately followed by 4625/4624 activity, may indicate credential reuse or backdoor reactivation.

title: Attempt to Change Password
description: An attempt was made to change an account password (self-service change).
operator_context: A privileged account whose password is changed outside policy may indicate takeover. Usually benign when performed by the account owner.

title: Reset Account Password
description: An administrator reset the password of an account.
operator_context: Admin resets of service accounts or privileged accounts are sensitive. An attacker resetting a password bypasses the need for the old one.

title: User Account Disabled
description: A user account was disabled.
operator_context: Disabling is standard offboarding. If followed by re-enable and logons, check whether the offboarding was authoritative.

title: User Account Deleted
description: A user account was deleted from the system.
operator_context: Deletions outside change control may attempt to remove evidence of created accounts. Verify against directory service logs.

title: Member Added to Security-Enabled Global Group
description: A member was added to a security-enabled global group (e.g., Domain Admins).
operator_context: Adding accounts to Domain Admins / Enterprise Admins is a prime lateral-movement + persistence target. Treat as high priority and validate authorization.

title: Member Removed from Security-Enabled Global Group
description: A member was removed from a security-enabled global group.
operator_context: Group removals can be used by attackers to lock out administrators during an intrusion. Verify the actor.

title: Member Added to Security-Enabled Local Group
description: A member was added to a security-enabled local group (e.g., Administrators, Remote Desktop Users).
operator_context: A non-admin account added to local Administrators or RDP Users enables direct takeover. Compare member lists against documented ownership.

title: Member Removed from Security-Enabled Local Group
description: A member was removed from a security-enabled local group.
operator_context: Usually legitimate hygiene. Verify the actor and reason within context of the machine's administrative model.

title: Security-Enabled Local Group Changed
description: A security-enabled local group was changed (name, membership, or settings).
operator_context: Follow-up membership read on the group to confirm no malicious member was added through a bulk change.

title: Security-Enabled Global Group Changed
description: A security-enabled global group was changed.
operator_context: Sensitive for admin groups. Re-read the group membership after the change to catch nested additions.

title: User Account Changed
description: A user account was changed (attributes modified).
operator_context: Changes to sensitive attributes (password reset flags, principal name, membership links) warrant review when performed by unexpected actors.

title: Account Lockout
description: A user account was locked out, typically after exceeding the failed-logon threshold.
operator_context: Cascading lockouts of an account across machines usually indicate password spraying or a credential leak. Identify the source IP from the paired 4625/4771 events before unlocking.

title: Computer Account Created
description: A computer account was created.
operator_context: Machine account creation corresponds to domain joins. Investigate unauthorized joins that bypass the provisioning process.

title: Computer Account Changed
description: A computer account was changed.
operator_context: Watch for changes to machine account attributes that could enable the machine to impersonate or receive delegated tickets.

title: Computer Account Deleted
description: A computer account was deleted.
operator_context: Deleting machine accounts is a destructive step used to disrupt or to cover lateral movement artifacts.

title: User Account Unlocked
description: A user account was manually unlocked by an administrator.
operator_context: Unlocking is part of lockout remediation. Chains of ignore -> relockout indicate an ongoing attack, not a user problem.

title: Kerberos TGT Requested
description: A Kerberos TGT ticket was requested for an account (initial authentication to the domain).
operator_context: Baseline to detect anomalous TGT volume (asymmetric kerberoast/S4U abuse). Watch for TGT requests with unusual encryption types or when RC4 is used by modern accounts.

title: Kerberos Service Ticket Requested
description: A Kerberos service ticket was requested for an account (used to access a service).
operator_context: Kerberoasting surface: requests for tickets for service accounts with weak passwords. Also a target for silver ticket forging after SPN enumeration.

title: Kerberos Pre-Authentication Failed
description: Kerberos pre-authentication failed, an indicator of a failed domain logon (wrong password / bad NTLM path).
operator_context: Equivalent to 4625 at the Kerberos level. Cluster by source address and account to detect password spray or AS-REP roasting attempts.

title: Credential Validation (NTLM)
description: The computer validated credentials for an NTLM logon (domain controller credential validation).
operator_context: Used to detect brute force on legacy/domain logons. A spike in credential validations from one workstation indicates password-spray against many accounts.

title: Account Name Changed
description: The name of an account was changed (user or machine account).
operator_context: Renaming hidden accounts is a persistence technique. Correlate the old name with prior audit activity.

title: Audit Log Cleared
description: The audit log was cleared, destroying the record of local security activity.
operator_context: Clearing security logs requires elevated privileges and is rarely legitimate. Immediate correlation with 4624/4688 before the clear is essential; consider centralized SIEM ingestion to survive the wipe.

title: Security Event Log Full / Cleared by Retention
description: The security event log was full and configured to overwrite events, losing older audit records.
operator_context: Log-overwrite policies destroy historical evidence. Increase log size, enable circular handling with longer retention, or centralize to a SIEM.

title: Operation Performed on AD Object
description: An operation was performed on an Active Directory object (read/write access to an object).
operator_context: Enables detection of sensitive object reads (DCSync precursor reads) when directory service auditing is enabled. Filter by object class and actor.

title: Directory Service Object Modified
description: An attribute of a directory service object was modified (e.g., DNS record, password-relevant attribute).
operator_context: Modifications to userAccountControl, pwdLastSet, or memberOf attributes are highest value; they can enable persistence or privilege escalation.

title: Directory Service Object Created
description: A directory service object was created (user, group, computer, container).
operator_context: Correlate with computer creation to detect unauthorized joins and with group creation to track shadow-privilege builds.

title: Directory Service Object Deleted
description: A directory service object was deleted (destructive AD change).
operator_context: Deleting objects can hide attacker-created accounts. Verify deletions against Change Management and restore from authoritative backup when unexpected.

title: Network Share Object Accessed
description: The root of a network share was accessed over SMB (file server path enumeration).
operator_context: Volumes of 5140 access from unexpected IPs indicate share enumeration during lateral movement reconnaissance.

title: Network Share Added
description: A network share was added on the system.
operator_context: Creating shares to temp or unusual paths is a data-exfiltration staging technique. Compare against documented share inventory.

title: Network Share Modified
description: A network share was modified (path or permissions changed).
operator_context: Permission broadening on a share (Everyone/Full control) to enable theft or ransomware staging. Verify ACL changes.

title: Network Share Deleted
description: A network share was deleted.
operator_context: Share deletion after staging files can clean up exfiltration paths. Look back for recent 5142/5143 on the same share name.

title: Detailed File Share Access
description: Detailed access to a file on a share when share-level auditing is enabled (includes relative path).
operator_context: Used to reconstruct exactly which files were accessed during data theft. Bulk enable on file servers that host sensitive shares.

title: Kernel-Power (Unexpected Reboot)
description: The system rebooted without a clean shutdown first, usually indicating a crash, power loss, or remote forced reset.
operator_context: Primary event for unplanned downtime. Correlate with 1001/1000 (crash minidump), kernel bugcheck dumps, and 6008 to identify whether the cause was hardware, power, or software.

title: System Shutdown Initiated
description: A process or user initiated a system shutdown with a reason code.
operator_context: Distinguish planned restarts (maintenance) from unexpected ones. Reason code + actor identify who triggered the shutdown.

title: Dashboard on Crash
description: The system detected a previous boot that crashed (recorded after the previous unclean shutdown).
operator_context: Confirms that the earlier 41/6008 event was a real crash; combine with memory.dmp analysis to identify the faulting driver.

title: Event Log Service Started
description: The Event Log service started, marking where the current event-log session begins on a boot.
operator_context: Marks machine boot in the System log. Useful as a baseline offset when reconstructing downtime windows.

title: Event Log Service Stopped (Clean Shutdown)
description: The Event Log service stopped, normally triggered by a clean shutdown.
operator_context: Presence of 6006 before a stop is a strong signal the shutdown was clean. Absence of 6006 before a 41/6008 indicates an unclean or forced reboot.

title: Unexpected Shutdown
description: The previous system shutdown at time X was unexpected (machine was not cleanly shut down).
operator_context: High-value uptime/availability indicator. Pairs with 41; use the embedded local/UTC timestamps to place the outage precisely.

title: Windows Up Time
description: The system has been up for a given duration; logged once shortly after each boot.
operator_context: Authoritative last-boot timestamp. Use to compute availability and to verify reboot times reported by 41/6008.

title: Service Failed to Start
description: The Service Control Manager could not start a service, with the specific error code provided.
operator_context: Common when dependents are missing, permissions are wrong, or the binary path is invalid. Check the error code, then verify the binary path and account permissions.

title: Service Depends on Missing Service
description: A service could not start because a service it depends on is missing, disabled, or failed.
operator_context: Walk the dependency chain: enable or start the prerequisite service. Watch for cascade failures after a security product or update is removed.

title: Service Timeout Connecting
description: A timeout was reached while waiting for a service to connect after being started.
operator_context: The service binary started but never signaled readiness within 30s. Investigate code-level hangs, high load, or blocked SCM notifications.

title: Service Timeout Responding
description: A timeout was reached while waiting for a service to respond to a service control request.
operator_context: Indicates a hung service that ignores stop/start control messages. Plan a controlled restart; repeated occurrences point to a code-level deadlock.

title: Service Hung on Start
description: A service hung during the start operation and did not report readiness.
operator_context: Hangs are often caused by startup waits on network, database, or mutex. Capture a snapshot at failure for diagnosis.

title: Service Terminated with Error
description: A service terminated unexpectedly with a specific error code.
operator_context: The service exit code explains cause. Cross-reference with Application-log events (1000/1001) for the underlying binary crash.

title: Service Terminated with Specific Error
description: A service terminated with a service-specific error not translated to a generic code.
operator_context: Check the vendor documentation for the exact service-specific error code. Often a configuration or licensing failure.

title: Service Terminated Unexpectedly
description: A service terminated unexpectedly and was restarted by SCM recovery actions (with recovery count).
operator_context: Recovery-action loop (nested crashes) indicates instability. Check the Application log for 1000/1001 from the service binary and consider disabling recovery if it masks the failure.

title: Service Crash (Terminated Unexpectedly)
description: A service terminated unexpectedly without an error code (hard crash).
operator_context: Indicates the service process exited abnormally (access violation, kill). Pair 7034 with Application log 1000/1001 to find the faulting module.

title: Service State Change
description: A service entered the running or stopped state.
operator_context: High-volume but essential for change detection: unexpected stops (maintenance windows), or starts of services that should never run, flag tampering. Baseline the noise.

title: Service Start Type Changed
description: The start type of a service was changed (e.g., manual to auto, or to disabled).
operator_context: Changes to auto-start are a persistence technique (service added to boot chain). Track every 7040 against change management.

title: Service Installed
description: A new service was installed on the system, including the service file name.
operator_context: Unexpected service installs are a signature persistence technique. Verify the binary path and the account; compare against the software inventory.

title: Application Error (Process Crash)
description: A process crashed with an unhandled exception; includes the faulting module, offset, and exception code.
operator_context: First stop for app crashes (e.g., w3wp.exe on IIS). Compare faulting module offsets across reports to detect repeatable bugs; enable WER dumps for deeper analysis.

title: Windows Error Reporting
description: Windows Error Reporting recorded details about a crash and optionally sent a report to Microsoft.
operator_context: Links the Application-log crash to the WER bucket (MiniDump file). Investigate if the dump is requested or if reports are suppressed for security-sensitive hosts.

title: Application Hang
description: A process stopped responding (window no longer responding) and was optionally terminated.
operator_context: Hangs usually precede crashes. Look for deadlocks, runaway threads, exhausted handles, and high IO on the host at the timestamp.

title: .NET Runtime Error
description: The .NET runtime reported an unhandled exception from a managed application.
operator_context: Provides CLR stack info. Use to flag hard-coded exceptions, missing assemblies, or CSP issues on .NET apps like those running on IIS.

title: Firewall Blocked a Packet (WFP)
description: The Windows Filtering Platform blocked a packet at the network layer (incoming/outgoing).
operator_context: Blocked packets to closed or denied ports are normal; voluminous blocks to a single dest port from one IP indicate port scanning or a misconfigured application.

title: Firewall Blocked a Connection (WFP)
description: The Windows Filtering Platform blocked a connection at the transport layer.
operator_context: Connection-level blocks fire when no rule permits the traffic. Review for legitimate services that are being tripped by the firewall ruleset.

title: Firewall Allowed a Connection (WFP)
description: The Windows Filtering Platform allowed a connection at the transport layer.
operator_context: Used to map permitted application traffic. Unexpected allowed connections (new binaries, unusual ports) reveal firewall-rule creep.

title: Firewall Blocked a Connection (Outbound)
description: The Windows Filtering Platform blocked an outbound connection.
operator_context: Outbound blocks to known-bad or unused destinations can indicate malware beaconing or a leaky application; investigate the source PID.

title: Firewall Allowed a Bind (WFP)
description: The Windows Filtering Platform allowed a local process to bind to a port.
operator_context: Monitor binds of unexpected processes to high or ephemeral ports (e.g., reverse-shell listener binds).

title: Firewall Blocked a Bind (WFP)
description: The Windows Filtering Platform blocked a process from binding to a local port.
operator_context: Blocked binds reveal applications trying to listen against policy — often malware staging a listener. Correlate the PID with 4688.

title: Defender Malware Detected
description: Microsoft Defender detected malware or potentially unwanted software on the system.
operator_context: Includes the threat name and severity. Correlate the file path with 4688/4104 for execution context; check whether it was quarantined (1117) or failed (1118/1119).

title: Defender Action Taken (Malware Removed)
description: Defender took remediation action (quarantine, remove, restore) on a detected threat.
operator_context: Success action. Review the action type and residual file path; a 'restore' with repeated detection indicates compromise persistence.

title: Defender Remediation Failed
description: Defender could not complete the remediation action on a threat (e.g., file in use).
operator_context: Files under active use may resist cleanup; schedule offline scan or manual removal. Persistent failures demand immediate containment.

title: Defender Threat Action Failed
description: Defender failed to perform the requested action on detected threat activity.
operator_context: A threat that survives action is a containment priority. Isolate the host and preserve the file for analysis.

title: Defender Blocked Execution (File)
description: Defender blocked execution of a file identified by behavior or reputation.
operator_context: File-execution block: correlate the hash with 4688 rollout and hunt for the same payload elsewhere (often part of an attack wave).

title: Defender Network Protection Blocked
description: Defender's Network Protection blocked a connection to a malicious domain or IP.
operator_context: Indicates an endpoint attempted a connection to a known-bad destination. Correlate with the process (4688) and pivot on the domain in proxy/DNS logs.

title: Defender Platform Update Installed
description: A new Defender platform version was installed on the endpoint.
operator_context: Track platform versions for consistency; version drift across fleets causes protection gaps.

title: Defender Definitions Updated
description: Defender security intelligence (definitions) was updated successfully.
operator_context: Monitor definition freshness; stale definitions on any endpoint = protection gap. Frequent successful updates are healthy.

title: Defender Real-Time Protection Disabled
description: Defender real-time protection was disabled, often due to group policy, tampering, or another AV.
operator_context: An unexpected RTP disable is a major red flag (tampering). Verify via policy; if no policy change, treat as compromise indicator.

title: Defender Scan Started
description: A Defender scan started (scheduled or user-initiated).
operator_context: On-demand scans outside the schedule may indicate manual investigation by an admin — or tampering to run cleanup. Note the trigger.

title: Defender Configuration Changed
description: A change was made to Defender settings (policy applied or manual tweak, including exclusion changes).
operator_context: Adding exclusions for temp/user paths is a common attacker step. Audit every 5007, especially exclusion additions.

title: Defender Real-Time Protection Enabled
description: Defender real-time protection was enabled.
operator_context: Expected after policy enforcement or post-tamper recovery. Verify the trigger and actor.

title: Defender Real-Time Protection Disabled (Tamper)
description: Defender real-time protection was disabled outside policy (event captured for tamper monitoring).
operator_context: Requires tamper-protection enforcement. If this fires without a policy change, escalate immediately.

title: PowerShell Module Logging
description: PowerShell module logging recorded pipeline command execution for enabled modules.
operator_context: Lighter-weight sibling of 4104. Use when full script block logging creates too much volume; still captures module-level command text.

title: PowerShell Script Block Logging
description: PowerShell recorded the full content of a script block being executed — the foundation of PowerShell forensics.
operator_context: Look for encoded command lines, Invoke-Expression on downloaded payloads, reflection into unmanaged code, and sensitive cmdlet families (Invoke-Mimikatz, Remove-MpPreference).

title: PowerShell Script Started
description: PowerShell began executing a script block (informational start message).
operator_context: Start marker for script lifetime. Combine with 4106 to compute execution duration and pair with 4104 content.

title: PowerShell Script Completed / Failed
description: PowerShell finished executing a script block; includes how long it ran and whether it completed.
operator_context: Records execution duration. Anomalous long-running scripts may indicate data staging or waiting on C2.

title: PowerShell Engine Started
description: Windows PowerShell engine started in a new process.
operator_context: High baseline volume; detect anomalous console-host combos and out-of-process launches (e.g., from Office macros).

title: PowerShell Engine Stopped
description: Windows PowerShell engine stopped.
operator_context: End marker for engine lifetime; useful to bound the activity window of a PowerShell payload.

title: PowerShell Provider Started
description: A specified PowerShell provider was started (e.g., Registry, FileSystem, Certificate).
operator_context: Provider starts to sensitive stores (Certificate, Registry) may indicate credential harvesting or persistence interaction.

title: PowerShell Pipeline Execution
description: Windows PowerShell pipeline execution detail (analytic trace of command invocation).
operator_context: Verbose trace; enable on selective hosts for deep command reconstruction when script block logging alone is insufficient or disabled.

title: Group Policy Processing Failed (No DC)
description: Group Policy processing failed because the computer could not obtain the domain controller name (network/DNS issue).
operator_context: Common after network flaps or DNS misconfiguration. Verify forward/reverse DNS resolution and DC reachability before redeploying policy.

title: Group Policy Processing Failed (Unknown Phase)
description: Group Policy processing failed during an unknown phase.
operator_context: Retry after resolving connectivity or SYSVOL issues; unify with 1054/1058 timestamps to pinpoint the failure phase.

title: Group Policy Processing Failed (File Access)
description: Windows cannot apply Group Policy because it failed to read a policy file (SYSVOL/permissions issue).
operator_context: Often SYSVOL DFSR lag, inaccessible GPO files, or permission regressions. Multi-client impact implies server-side SYSVOL problem.

title: Group Policy DNS Lookup Failed
description: Group Policy could not be processed because DNS lookup for the domain/DC failed.
operator_context: Root cause is DNS; check DC SRV records, preferred DNS server config, and connectivity to resolve the FQDN.

title: DNS Name Resolution Timed Out
description: Name resolution for a record timed out after the configured retry count.
operator_context: Frequent timeouts indicate upstream DNS latency or a poisoned/cached stale record. Identify the failing name and reduce TTL churn.

title: DNS Name Resolution Failed
description: Name resolution for a record failed permanently (no valid response).
operator_context: Check the queried domain validity, forwarders, and whether it matches blocked-list patterns. Persistent failure on a critical FQDN = incident.

title: DNS Server Failed to Open Socket
description: The DNS server was unable to open a socket for listening; often a port conflict with another DNS server instance.
operator_context: Check for multiple DNS services bound to UDP/TCP 53 (e.g., conflicting with a proxy or second DNS role).

title: DNS Server Unable to Register with AD
description: The DNS server could not dynamically register its SRV/A records with the Active Directory domain for its zone.
operator_context: Breaks domain discovery; check DS-backed zone status, secure dynamic updates permission, and replication health.

title: DNS Server Failed to Load Zones
description: The DNS server was unable to load or read one or more zones from AD or disk.
operator_context: Zone load failure may indicate a corrupt zone database, AD replication snapshot inconsistencies, or read permission regression.

title: DHCP Address Lease Renewed
description: A DHCPv4 client successfully obtained a lease (IP address) for the interface.
operator_context: Lease renewal success. Sudden renewals at a different server (rogue DHCP) can be detected by comparing lease server IPs.

title: DHCP Address Lease Lost / Renewal Failed
description: The DHCPv4 client lost its lease or could not renew, leaving the machine without a valid IPv4 address.
operator_context: Causes connectivity outage; check DHCP server health, scope exhaustion, and network segmentation after the event.

title: TCP Auto-Tuning Changed
description: The TCP auto-tuning level was modified, commonly as a fix for high-throughput or packet-loss issues.
operator_context: Non-standard tuning levels can degrade throughput; document who changed TCP stack parameters and why.

title: TCP/IP Half-Open Connection Limit Saturated
description: The TCP/IP half-open connection limit was reached, usually from connection attempts being queued.
operator_context: Indicates connection saturation: heavy outbound connections (P2P, malware propagation) or inbound SYN floods.

title: Disk Error (Ntfs/Storage)
description: The disk reported an error (bad block, controller communication problem).
operator_context: Predictive failure signal. Check SMART data, backup immediately, and schedule hardware replacement before data loss.

title: Paging Error (Disk IO Failure)
description: An error was detected on the paging file / disk during read/write operation.
operator_context: Disk hardware failure during paging can freeze the machine; check cables/controller and replace immediately.

title: NTFS File System Corruption
description: The NTFS file system structure on the disk is corrupt, and the system is degrading gracefully (read-only).
operator_context: High severity: run chkdsk, evaluate the disk with SMART, and restore from backup if the volume is unrecoverable.

title: Volume Corruption Detected (VSS/ReFS)
description: Volume-level integrity issue detected, either by NTFS or the resiliency layer.
operator_context: Investigate volume health and backup integrity. On ReFS, enable integrity streams and rebuild degraded storage pools.

title: Disk Driver Reset
description: A device reset was issued to the disk after a timeout or bus error.
operator_context: A reset is the last resort before the device fails; track frequency — increasing resets forecast controller or cable failure.

title: Paging Operation Failed
description: A paging read/write operation failed, usually caused by disk failure.
operator_context: A host with failing paging will become unstable; plan maintenance immediately.

title: Disk IO Retried then Succeeded
description: A disk I/O operation was retried and succeeded (transient error recovered).
operator_context: A leading indicator of mechanical/cable issues before a hard failure. Baseline frequencies per host.

title: VSS Shadow Copy Failure
description: Volume Shadow Copy failed (snapshot creation aborted), commonly breaking backups.
operator_context: Check VSS writers status (vssadmin list writers), disk space, and third-party filters. Persistent failures make backups non-restorable — restore the snapshot chain.

title: Resource Exhaustion (Low Memory)
description: Windows diagnosed a low virtual-memory condition; identifies the process consuming the most memory.
operator_context: Tune memory pressure: increase RAM/swap or identify a leaky process. Frequent events degrade performance and can crash services.

title: Low Memory Condition Persisted
description: The low-memory condition identified earlier continues to persist.
operator_context: Persistent pressure means the leak outpaces swap. Validate the reported process and plan reallocation or restart.

title: Scheduled Task Completed
description: A scheduled task completed execution successfully.
operator_context: Completion of tasks that should not run (or at anomalous times) indicates persistence deployment or compromise.

title: Scheduled Task Missed
description: A scheduled task did not run at its scheduled start time.
operator_context: Missed runs break maintenance/AV/backup duty. Check system sleep, service account, and task conditions.

title: Scheduled Task Action Failed
description: A task action failed (command/script returned a non-zero code).
operator_context: Failed task actions to temp paths or with encoded arguments should be treated as suspicious regardless of schedule.

title: Scheduled Task Started
description: A scheduled task started running.
operator_context: Track the start of tasks executed under high-privilege accounts; correlate the action command with 4688.

title: Scheduled Task Triggered
description: A scheduled task was triggered by schedule, event, or manual run.
operator_context: Manual/by-trigger runs of otherwise-scheduled tasks outside their pattern are a persistence/takedown signal.

title: Scheduled Task Created (Security)
description: A scheduled task was created, captured via audit policy.
operator_context: Task creation is a classic persistence vector (highest privilege + encoded commands). Audit the action command and the account creating it.

title: Scheduled Task Deleted (Security)
description: A scheduled task was deleted.
operator_context: Deleting task artifacts can be part of cleaning evidence. Correlate with prior 4698 of the same command.

title: Scheduled Task Enabled (Security)
description: A scheduled task was enabled.
operator_context: Enabling previously disabled tasks may activate dormant persistence. Verify the action and schedule fields.

title: Scheduled Task Disabled (Security)
description: A scheduled task was disabled.
operator_context: Disabling a defense/AV/monitoring task is an evasion step observed before many attacks.

title: Scheduled Task Updated (Security)
description: A scheduled task was updated (trigger, action, or settings changed).
operator_context: Updating an existing benign task to run a malicious command is stealthier than creating one. Diff the action field against prior state.

title: WMI Activity Logged
description: WMI activity occurred (namespace/component operation) during normal provider operation.
operator_context: Fluorescent baseline; focus on WMI activity from unusual processes (wmic.exe, PowerShell Invoke-WmiMethod) for lateral movement detection.

title: WMI Activity Error
description: WMI activity logged an error (provider crash, denied access, or malformed query).
operator_context: Repeated provider errors can break management tooling and integrity monitoring; check for a poisoned provider or corruption.

title: WMI Permanent Event Subscription Registered
description: A permanent WMI event consumer (subscription/filter) was registered — a persistence and collection mechanism.
operator_context: WMI subscriptions run commands on boot/interval and rarely have admin approval at endpoints. Enumerate known-good subscriptions and flag every new one.

title: WMI Permanent Event Subscription (Detailed)
description: Detailed record of a WMI permanent event subscription, including the consumer command.
operator_context: The consumer command reveals the payload (e.g., PowerShell encoded string). Pivot from the subscription name to 4688/4104 events.

title: Hyper-V Virtual Machine Started
description: A Hyper-V virtual machine entered the running state.
operator_context: Track VM lifecycle; unexpected start of a VM (e.g., exfiltration appliance) or sudden stop indicates administrative tampering.

title: Hyper-V Virtual Machine Stopped
description: A Hyper-V virtual machine exited the running state (stopped/ended).
operator_context: Unexpected VM stops can be caused by host memory pressure, storage loss, or vmmem crash. Correlate with 18500 (guest kernel panic).

title: Hyper-V Heartbeat Lost / Guest Down
description: The guest operating system heartbeat was lost, indicating the VM is unresponsive or crashed.
operator_context: Heartbeat loss = guest kernel hang or DoS. Inspect guest memory dump and the host's resource usage at the timestamp.

title: RDP Session Logon
description: A remote desktop session was successfully logged on (protocol plus source source address when logged).
operator_context: Prime RDP evidence: correlate session logons with 4624 Logon Type 10 and the source IP. Unexpected RDP logons from external or off-VLAN IPs are high-value alerts.

title: RDP Session Remote Logoff
description: A remote desktop session was logged off remotely.
operator_context: Remote logoffs mark session end; combine with 21 to measure session length for anomalous-looking full-shift sessions.

title: RDP Session Logged Off
description: A remote desktop session was logged off (session terminated).
operator_context: Session close marker; frequent short sessions from one source pattern indicate automation or credential cycling.

title: RDP Session Disconnected
description: A remote desktop session was disconnected while the session remained active.
operator_context: Disconnect-without-logon keeps the session alive and can be used to persist access. Watch for high disconnect/reconnect cycles.

title: RDP Session Reconnected
description: A remote desktop session was reconnected.
operator_context: Reconnect to an already-open session from a different IP is a session-hijacking indicator.

title: DCOM Default Permission Denied
description: The application-specific permission settings do not grant local activation permission for a DCOM server.
operator_context: Noisy but persistent 10016s indicate misconfigured DCOM identities; reconcile component-services ACLs or suppress known-benign combinations.
